data.title: bn-1hape: OS entropy, local keystore, daemon receipt signing

data.body: [risk:high] Existing-store reads do not secure the keystore directory or bind permission checks to opened descriptors. require_private checks each pathname first. read_audit and read_key later reopen those pathnames. File::open follows replacements and symlinks. open also never checks directory mode or owner. A local user with directory write access can swap both checked files for readable attacker-controlled files. The daemon can then sign with an attacker-known identity. Failure modes: signing-identity substitution, forged audit history, persistent refusal, or key-path redirection. Edge cases: world-writable directories, writable parents, symlinked directories, ownership mismatch, concurrent rename, and privileged service users. Rollback: disable receipt signing and restore the keystore from a trusted snapshot. Do not remint over the existing store. Monitoring: report directory and file owner, mode, inode, and path-type mismatches before key use. Validation: test unsafe directory modes, foreign ownership, symlink components, and deterministic rename races around both opens. Fix by anchoring reads to a verified directory descriptor. Reject symlinks and verify owner, mode, and regular-file status on opened descriptors. The separate risk:critical human-approval gate remains required.

[risk:medium] The 16 MiB encoded-byte cap does not bound decoded allocation. Value::decode materializes the complete arbitrary Value before replay checks record shape. A near-limit sequence of scalar values can expand to hundreds of MiB and terminate a constrained daemon. Apply a strict record-count or decoded-allocation bound before full materialization. Add an adversarial amplification test.

data.reason: BLOCK: risk:high keystore path replacement can substitute an attacker-known signing identity. risk:medium audit decoding permits large allocation amplification. The risk:critical human-approval gate remains separate.

data.body: Fixed in 56eb35d. Each file is lstat-examined (symlink -> SymlinkedFile), opened once with O_NOFOLLOW (per-target constant; where unknown, the dev/inode check still refuses a followed link), then validated on the opened descriptor via fstat: same dev/inode as examined (Swapped), regular file (NotRegular), owner == expected uid (ForeignOwner), no group/other bits (InsecurePermissions). Key and audit are read from those descriptors. Store dir: not a symlink (SymlinkedStore), a directory (NotADirectory), owned by the uid (ForeignOwner), not group/world-writable (UnsafeDirectory); ancestors must not be writable unless sticky (UnsafeParent), otherwise trusted (documented boundary). Existing dirs are never tightened or re-minted over. Owner = /proc/self uid on Linux, or LocalKeystore::expecting_owner (also the foreign-owner test seam). Tests: writable dir, foreign owner, symlinked key, symlinked dir, writable ancestor, O_NOFOLLOW, and swap_after_open_reads_the_original_descriptor (rename-after-open seam; a fresh open then sees the attacker key, proving the swap happened).

Fixed in 56eb35d. The audit log is now framed: AUDIT_MAGIC, a count capped at MAX_AUDIT_RECORDS (4096), then each record length-prefixed and capped at MAX_AUDIT_RECORD_LEN (1024). The keystore decodes one record at a time from the bound descriptor, shape-checks it, and applies it with the new SigningRegistry::replay_record, so no whole-log Value is materialized. a_hostile_audit_log_is_refused_within_a_memory_limit runs in a ulimit -v 256 MiB child: a max-size log of amplifying null sequences, an oversize count, an oversize record length, and the old 16 MiB single-value attack are all refused.

[risk:high] Re-review at 56eb35d: fixed. Failure modes now fail closed as typed store, owner, path, swap, replay, restore, or signing refusals; a crash between file writes leaves Incomplete, and an unconfigured daemon remains explicitly unsigned. Edge cases reviewed: leaf and file symlinks, foreign ownership, writable directories and ancestors, rename races, truncated or oversized records, and revoked signers. Rollback: remove the receipt_signer configuration and restore the keystore from a trusted snapshot; never mint over an incomplete store. Monitoring: alert on KeystoreError variants, signing refusal, and unexpected unsigned receipts. Validation: the persisted range includes descriptor-bound swap tests, symlink and ownership tests, bounded hostile-log tests, and end-to-end sign and tamper tests. Any separate risk:critical human approval remains mandatory; this LGTM cannot replace it.

[risk:medium] Re-review at 56eb35d: fixed. The framed audit format caps the record count and each encoded record, decodes one record at a time, applies it incrementally, and rejects trailing bytes. The hostile-log test covers the prior amplification shape under a constrained address space.

data.reason: Verified fixed at 56eb35d: descriptor-bound reads, owner and directory checks, and fail-closed typed refusals.
Verified fixed at 56eb35d: bounded framed record-at-a-time replay.

Reviewed the full persisted range fa2cdf9..56eb35d across all 23 changed files. The descriptor-bound keystore fix and bounded audit replay close both prior findings. No security blocker remains. This vote does not replace any separately required human approval.
